text:
sophie: Draft of the product launch blog + bench snapshot is up — PTAL: https://docs.redwood.ai/launch/draft
matt: Awesome, posting now. Quick ask — can you paste the short benchmark callouts here so I can sanity-check claims? 
kevin: Hero feels a bit heavy on engineering speak. maybe simplify "optimized runtime" -> "faster responses" :thinking_face:

sophie: Good call. Pasted the bench highlights below (kept them conservative):
```
- Latency: 15–30ms p50 for common prompts (hosted)
- Cost: ~0.9 tokens/s dollar-equivalent improvement vs baseline model X
- Throughput: 2.5x steady-state with batching & KV-cache
```

devon: Ops look OK. Inbound lead routing mapping looks clear but please add UTM examples for webinar CTAs so we can map traffic in HubSpot.

sophie: Adding UTMs now. Proposed CTA routing matrix snippet:
```
CTA A -> webinar-signups (utm_source=blog&utm_campaign=launch_ctaA)
CTA B -> product-demo (utm_source=blog&utm_campaign=launch_ctaB)
```

jenny: Prefer CTA B in hero to drive demos — historically higher MQL rate from demo CTAs.
kevin: +1 on CTA B in hero, keep a secondary inline "watch webinar" link for nurture.

ella: Legal quick note — flag on claim "0.9 tokens/s dollar-equivalent improvement". Need citation or reword to "up to" or add footnote referencing benchmark appendix.

sophie: ok rewording to "up to 0.9x unit-cost improvement on typical LLM workloads" and adding appendix link. updated live doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/launch/draft#benchmarks

legalbot: @ella Legal review requested on 1714242424: bench claim language change. Please review within 48 hours.

devon: Also, operations: can we add one fallback routing rule for Dedicated -> Hosted in case capacity is constrained? small config note in ops runbook would be great.

sophie: noted — adding runbook snippet and fallback policy. Will lock copy after legal OK. Target: final sign-off by EOD for ops handoff tomorrow morning.

matt: thanks — I'll prepare the social blurbs once copy is locked. prefer we keep one tech-forward quote and one product-forward quote.

sophie: copying the two quote variants into the doc now. Thanks all :thumbsup:
